architecture.title: AFDD triage — facts from code, judgment from Jev, decisions from policy
architecture.caption: Code validates the BMS reading and computes stale / bad_quality / deviation. Jev sees the operator note plus those facts and proposes a queue, a safety signal and a severity. A deterministic policy overrides the queue on bad data and ORs the safety signal with a keyword backstop. Nothing is written to the building.

sequence.title: Lab 07-2 — one call, four outcomes
sequence.caption: Jev is asked about the note once. Four telemetry situations then flow through the same deterministic policy, producing different queues without another model call.

charts.title: Same 'No smoke' note — the wording decides
charts.caption: Measured by labs/lab02_what_if.py (jev-1.13.0). 'No smoke' literally mentions smoke. Test negations explicitly, and keep a deterministic backstop for safety.

charts.title: Five incidents — safety probability vs the 0.20 review line
charts.caption: Measured by labs/lab01_triage_incidents.py. Even an explicit 'burning smell' scored 0.73, not ~1 — which is why the safety threshold is low (0.20) and OR'd with a keyword check.
